answers.reason: The student holds no office and does not decide on university-wide statutes and strategy.
The student is not responsible for university budget allocation.
The student holds no office and is not involved in selecting professors.
Ordinary students are represented by the elected student representative and do not hold seats in the faculty council.
Student representation in formal teaching committees is handled by the elected student representative rather than an ordinary student.
Although it decides on individual students' matters, an ordinary student without office does not sit on the board that adjudicates credit recognition and appeals.
The student is enrolled in a bachelor programme and is not involved in awarding research grants.
Rewriting module descriptions is a task for teaching staff and elected representatives rather than an ordinary student without office.
The student is not responsible for procuring laboratory equipment.
Planning the orientation week for new students is the single informal student matter where an ordinary student without office takes part.
